title: Activation ledger: replay and effect scan fail closed at scale
description:
Objective: make the activation ledger's replay and effect-binding lookups keep answering as the store grows and as the aggregate accumulates its Foundation tail.

RAISED BY: governor-18a42000 adversarial audit of today's diff, 2026-08-15 (7 lenses, 35 findings raised, 36 independent skeptic verdicts). Both defects below are in task-df29871b "Durable activation authority ledger", which is DONE and QA-approved with a mutation-drilled retry. Both survived adversarial refutation and I re-verified each on current bytes myself. FILED AS ONE TASK deliberately: both live in the activation-ledger reader/commit pair, and two tasks editing activation-ledger-reader.ts concurrently would collide in this shared worktree.

DEFECT 1 — REPLAY FEEDS A WHOLE AGGREGATE TO AN EXACTLY-ONE READER (HIGH).
apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-commit.ts:140-144:
    events = store.readEvents(aggregateId);
    const durable = readActivationLedgerRecord(aggregateId, events);
apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-reader.ts:61:
    if (events.length > 1) return activationLedgerUnknown("ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS");
`answerReplayed` hands EVERY event on the aggregate to a reader whose second guard refuses more than one. The moment any second event exists on that aggregate — the Foundation launch tail is the obvious source — the idempotent re-commit path refuses AMBIGUOUS instead of returning the stored record. Idempotency is precisely the property that must survive a growing aggregate. Note that foundation-launch-authority.ts:36 imports a DIFFERENT reader, `readFoundationActivationHistory`, which handles history; the replay path appears to be using the wrong one of the two.

DEFECT 2 — EFFECT SCAN DIES PERMANENTLY PAST 6,400 EVENTS (HIGH).
apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-reader.ts:107:
    const MAX_SCAN_PAGES = 64, SCAN_PAGE_SIZE = 100, MAX_QUERY_CHARS = 400;
`scanForEffect` pages the GLOBAL event stream via `store.readEventsAfter(cursor, SCAN_PAGE_SIZE)` from cursor 0n, and it CANNOT return early on a hit because it must prove the match unique — its only success exit is `if (!read.hasMore) return { aggregateId: found, refusal: null }` at :255. So it must exhaust the entire stream every call. Once the project's global event count exceeds 64 x 100 = 6,400, `read.hasMore` is still true when the loop at :237 finishes its 64 iterations, control falls through to `return no("FOUNDATION_BINDING_SCAN_INCOMPLETE")` at :260, and `readCurrentEffectSessionBinding` stops finding ANY activation — permanently, for every effect, with no recovery and no operator signal beyond that one code.

This is a time bomb rather than an edge case: the global event count only grows, the bound is on TOTAL project events rather than per-effect, and it fails closed into a refusal that looks like a legitimate authority answer. A green suite cannot see it because no test store reaches 6,400 events.

NOT IN SCOPE: changing the durable event format, the ledger's digest/seal discipline, the exactly-one guarantee itself where it is genuinely required, or foundation-launch-authority's own admission guards. If the right answer is an index or a per-aggregate query rather than a global scan, that is a design decision worth raising rather than assuming.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test.
definitionOfDone: An idempotent re-commit returns the stored durable record on an aggregate that carries its Foundation launch tail. A test commits, appends the tail so the aggregate holds more than one event, re-commits with the same idempotency key, and asserts the ORIGINAL record is returned - not ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS and not a caller-supplied echo.

The exactly-one guarantee is preserved where it is genuinely required: a test proves a genuinely ambiguous aggregate still refuses with its exact stable code and layer, so defect 1's fix narrows the reader's input rather than weakening the guard.

readCurrentEffectSessionBinding answers correctly on a store holding more than 6,400 events. A test drives a store past that boundary with a real file-backed SqliteEventStore, asserts the binding is FOUND, and pins the event count it was proven at with a literal so a later change to page size or page count cannot silently shrink the coverage.

The uniqueness property the scan exists to prove still holds at scale: a second matching activation past the old 6,400 bound is still detected and refused with the exact FOUNDATION_BINDING_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS code and its layer, proving the fix did not buy scale by giving up the invariant.

Mutation drills prove both guards are attached to production: restoring the whole-aggregate read into the exactly-one reader turns a NAMED test red, and independently restoring the 64-page bound turns a NAMED test red on the past-6400 case. Each drill is restored byte-exact and verified by hash.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test exits 0 with each leg's exit code read separately, and every existing activation-ledger test stays green and unmodified.
taskRails: Both defects fail CLOSED into refusals that look like legitimate authority answers. Fixing them must not weaken any invariant: the exactly-one guarantee and the scan's uniqueness proof both still have to hold. Buying scale by dropping a uniqueness check is a wrong answer.

Assert the reason code and the layer, never merely that the call failed or succeeded. Where two layers can refuse the same input, the test states which one answered - both of these defects are cases of the WRONG refusal winning.

Any test that proves behaviour at scale must pin the event count it was proven at as a literal. A later reduction in page size or page count must break that test rather than silently shrink the proof.

Do not change the durable event format, the digest/seal discipline, or foundation-launch-authority's admission guards. If the correct fix is an index or a per-aggregate query instead of a global scan, raise that as a design decision rather than landing it unannounced.

Re-measure both sites on current bytes before editing - activation-ledger-commit.ts:140-144 and activation-ledger-reader.ts:61/107/237/255/260 were measured today, but this is a shared worktree with live agents. Preserve foreign work and commit only explicit owned paths.
Keep each production source under 250 physical lines, split before 400, and measure with grep -c '' rather than PowerShell Measure-Object, which undercounts.

TEST-SURFACE FACTS FOR STEPS 2/4. Store: MAX_EVENTS_PER_COMMIT = 256, MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 1000 (store-contracts.ts:22,26) — 6,400+ filler events need >=26 `store.commit` calls, each its own transaction; a single 6,500-event commit is rejected. `SqliteEventStore.commit(CommitInput)` takes `{aggregateId, commandBytes, commandId, committedAt, events: EventDraft[], expectedVersion}` so filler can be spread over distinct aggregates each at expectedVersion 0. scanForEffect `continue`s on any non-EffectActivationCommitted eventType, so filler events are skipped, but EVERY activation-typed event must be well-formed or the scan refuses MALFORMED. Foundation tail types available via `FOUNDATION_TRANSITION_EVENT_TYPES` + `encodeFoundationTransition` (foundation-activation-transition.ts:31,214). implementationPlan.description:
TDD FOR DEFECT 1 — write both tests first, in `apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-commit.test.ts`.

TEST A (DoD 1), the reproduction: commit an activation, then APPEND A FOREIGN EVENT to the same aggregate so it holds more than one event, then re-commit with the same idempotency key. Assert the ORIGINAL stored record is returned with disposition REPLAYED — not ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS, and not a caller-supplied echo. Prove it is the STORED record by re-committing with the same key but different record bytes and requiring the stored bytes to win.

CONSTRUCT THE TAIL DIRECTLY. Defect 1 is latent — `createFoundationClaudeLauncher` has zero callers — so a test that waits for a live Foundation path to append the tail will never exercise the defect and will pass vacuously.

TEST B (DoD 2), the guard that must NOT weaken: an aggregate carrying TWO ACTIVATION events still refuses with the exact ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS code and its layer, asserted literally. This is the test that distinguishes a correct fix (narrow the input) from a wrong one (relax the count check). Without it, "take the first event" passes Test A while destroying the ledger's core guarantee.

Both assert code AND layer, never merely that the call failed — two layers can refuse here and these defects are precisely cases of the wrong refusal winning.

Test A fails now; Test B passes now and must still pass after step 3.

implementationPlan.description:
FIX DEFECT 1 — narrow the reader's input, in `apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-commit.ts` (or the reader, whichever keeps the invariant clearest).

Select the ACTIVATION events before the exactly-one check. The discriminator is already in the module — `ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVENT_TYPE`, used at reader.ts:65 one line after the count guard — so filtering by it is applying an existing rule at the right moment, not inventing a new one.

AFTER THE FIX THE GUARD MUST STILL MEAN "exactly one activation record per aggregate":
- zero activation events -> ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVIDENCE_ABSENT (unchanged)
- two activation events -> ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS (unchanged; step 2's Test B pins it)
- one activation event plus any number of foreign events -> the record (this is the fix)

DO NOT relax `events.length > 1` to "take the first", and do not swap in `readFoundationActivationHistory` (:161) wholesale — the replay path needs ONE record with exactly-one semantics, not a history.

Preserve the digest cross-check at :150: `answerReplayed` re-seals the durable record and refuses ACTIVATION_LEDGER_REPLAY_DIVERGED when it differs from the candidate. That is what stops a replay from echoing the caller, and it must survive untouched.

Run both step-2 tests: A must now pass, B must still pass. Run the whole existing activation-ledger suite — DoD 6 requires every existing test green and UNMODIFIED.
implementationPlan.note:
DEFECT 1 FIXED by narrowing the reader's INPUT at the call site in activation-ledger-commit.ts `answerReplayed`:

    const activations = events.filter(
      (event) => event.eventType === ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVENT_TYPE,
    );
    const durable = readActivationLedgerRecord(aggregateId, activations);

ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVENT_TYPE was ALREADY imported in this module (it names the event type on the commit path), so no new import.

WHY THE FILTER IS IN commit.ts AND NOT IN THE READER - this is the load-bearing design decision and it is forced, not preferred. `readActivationLedgerRecord`'s contract is "these events are the whole evidence", and its existing REFUSALS table in activation-ledger-reader.test.ts pins a lone wrong-typed event to ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVENT_TYPE_UNEXPECTED. Filtering INSIDE the reader would narrow that singleton to zero events and silently answer ABSENT instead, reddening an existing test - a DoD 6 violation and a real loss of discrimination for the reader's other two callers (`readFoundationActivationHistory` at reader.ts:184 and `scanForEffect`, both of which already pass a correct SINGLETON). Narrowing at the one call site that was over-supplying is the minimal correct change.

POST-FIX SEMANTICS, exactly as the plan specified:
- zero activation events -> ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVIDENCE_ABSENT (unchanged)
- two activation events -> ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS (unchanged; Test B pins it)
- one activation + any number of foreign events -> the record (the fix)

`events.length > 1` was NOT relaxed. `readFoundationActivationHistory` was NOT swapped in. The digest cross-check that refuses ACTIVATION_LEDGER_REPLAY_DIVERGED is untouched and is now pinned on a TAILED aggregate too, by the new A2 test.

implementationPlan.description:
FIX DEFECT 2 — remove the false ceiling, in `apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-reader.ts`.

Stop bounding `scanForEffect` by page COUNT. The loop already terminates without that cap: an empty page with `hasMore` returns SCAN_INCOMPLETE (:242), and a cursor that does not strictly advance returns SCAN_INCOMPLETE (:258-259). A stalled, lying or broken store is caught by those guards, so `MAX_SCAN_PAGES = 64` provides no safety a correct store needs — it only imposes an arbitrary 6,400-event ceiling that fails closed into a refusal indistinguishable from a real authority answer.

KEEP THE UNIQUENESS PROOF INTACT (task rail 1). The scan still may not return early on a hit: it must keep walking to detect a second distinct aggregateId and refuse FOUNDATION_BINDING_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS. Step 4's Test D is the check.

Keep `SCAN_PAGE_SIZE` as the page size. If `MAX_SCAN_PAGES` becomes unreferenced, remove it rather than leaving a constant nothing reads — an unread bound reads to the next maintainer as an enforced limit.

DO NOT grow this file toward 400 lines; it is already 328. If the change needs meaningful new code, extract a helper module with its own `.js` bridge instead.

RAISE THE DESIGN QUESTION, do not solve it here (task rail 4). Even fixed, the scan is O(total project events) PER LOOKUP because it reads the global stream from cursor 0n and cannot exit early. Write that finding down and FILE A FOLLOW-UP TASK for a per-effect index or per-aggregate query, recording its id in the handoff. Landing an index unannounced is explicitly forbidden; leaving the performance cliff unrecorded just moves the time bomb.

Run Tests C and D; both must pass. Run the whole existing suite — every existing test green and unmodified.
implementationPlan.note:
DEFECT 2 FIXED in activation-ledger-reader.ts. Two edits, both minimal:

1. Constant line :107 `const MAX_SCAN_PAGES = 64, SCAN_PAGE_SIZE = 100, MAX_QUERY_CHARS = 400;` -> `const SCAN_PAGE_SIZE = 100, MAX_QUERY_CHARS = 400;`. MAX_SCAN_PAGES is REMOVED, not left unreferenced - an unread bound reads to the next maintainer as an enforced limit. Verified: `grep -n MAX_SCAN_PAGES apps/daemon/src/activation/*.ts` now matches only one line, a HISTORY comment inside foundation-launch-authority.test.ts explaining what the pinned literal 6,400 refers to. Zero production references remain.

2. `for (let page = 0; page < MAX_SCAN_PAGES; page += 1)` -> `for (;;)`, and the now-unreachable post-loop `return no("FOUNDATION_BINDING_SCAN_INCOMPLETE")` deleted (the loop has no normal exit, so leaving it would not have compiled cleanly as reachable code).

TERMINATION IS UNCHANGED AND STILL OWNED BY THE TWO EXISTING GUARDS, which is the whole reason removing the cap is safe:
- `if (read.hasMore && read.items.length === 0) return no("FOUNDATION_BINDING_SCAN_INCOMPLETE")` - a store that claims more but yields nothing.
- `const next = read.nextCursor; if (next === null || next <= cursor) return no("FOUNDATION_BINDING_SCAN_INCOMPLETE")` - a cursor that does not STRICTLY advance.
Both fire on the FIRST bad page, i.e. strictly sooner than a 64-page cap would. Both are already pinned by the pre-existing test "reports a scan it cannot finish as SCAN_INCOMPLETE and a throw as UNREADABLE" (its `stuck` and `stalled` fakes), which stayed green and unmodified. A stalled, lying or throwing store therefore still terminates and still refuses.

UNIQUENESS PROOF INTACT (task rail 1). No early return was added. The only success exit is still `if (!read.hasMore) return { aggregateId: found, refusal: null }`, and the second-distinct-aggregate check still refuses FOUNDATION_BINDING_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS. A comment now states why there is no early return, so the next maintainer does not "optimise" it away.

SCAN_PAGE_SIZE kept as the page size. Durable event format, digest/seal discipline and foundation-launch-authority's admission guards all untouched.

FILE SIZE: activation-ledger-reader.ts 328 -> 335 lines. Net +7 (the cap's removal is a deletion; the growth is explanatory comment, which I tightened from an initial 338). Under the 400 split point and not meaningfully closer to it; no helper module extraction was warranted for a two-line change.

CORRECTION FROM THE AUTHOR (governor-18a42000), posted minutes after filing. THE TWO DEFECTS DIFFER IN REACHABILITY, and I stated both as live. One is; one is latent. Read this before planning — it changes how you reproduce defect 1.

My two skeptics DISAGREED on defect 1. One confirmed the mechanics in forensic detail; the other returned "MECHANICS CONFIRMED, REACHABILITY REFUTED". I re-measured myself rather than taking either.

DEFECT 1 (replay -> ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS) IS LATENT, NOT LIVE:
- `createFoundationLauncherAuthority` has NO caller outside its own module.
- Its only composition point is `createFoundationClaudeLauncher` (foundation-launch-authority.ts:290), which has ZERO callers anywhere in apps/ or packages/, tests included.
- It is NOT exported from the daemon root — `apps/daemon/src/index.ts` returns zero hits for it.
- A positive control on the identical query shape (`createStoreDependencies` -> daemon-store-dependencies.ts:92, :167, mcp-http-main.ts:5) confirms the greps are well scoped, so these zeros are real absences.

So nothing in production can append the Foundation transition tail today, which means the aggregate never reaches 2+ events, which means the replay path cannot currently return AMBIGUOUS. The defect is real code with correct mechanics and NO live trigger.

WHEN IT ACTIVATES, AND WHY THAT MATTERS RIGHT NOW: `createFoundationClaudeLauncher`'s own doc comment names its consumer — "The composed launcher task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9 consumes." task-6cbff010 (Durable Claude attempt dispatch) is the keystone gating roughly nine downstream tasks and is in PLANNING today. **The moment task-6cbff010 lands its consumer edge, this defect goes live** — and it will present as an actively-launching activation reporting itself unverifiable on every retry. Fixing it before that edge lands is strictly cheaper than debugging it after.

DEFECT 2 (6,400-event scan bound) IS LIVE. `readCurrentEffectSessionBinding` has a real production caller: apps/daemon/src/coordination/coordination-adapter.ts:27 imports it and :218 calls it. That path is composed today. The time-bomb framing in the description stands unchanged.

CONSEQUENCES FOR YOUR PLAN:
- Defect 2 is the urgent half. Do not let defect 1's unreachability delay it.
- For defect 1, you CANNOT reproduce the failure through a production entry point today. Drive it at the adapter seam by appending a second event to the aggregate directly, and say plainly in your evidence that the trigger is not yet composed. Do NOT manufacture a fake consumer edge to make it reproducible — that would be reimplementing authority in a test, which Clause 2 forbids.
- If you judge that defect 1 should instead be deferred and re-filed against task-6cbff010's landing, that is a defensible call. Say so in writing rather than silently dropping it; a half-fix that leaves one clause unaddressed is the exact pattern that produced task-70b6361d earlier today.

The daemon also warned on this task's title ("contains 'and' — often two tasks wearing one title"). That warning now looks better founded than my rationale for bundling: the halves have different urgency and different reproduction paths. I bundled to avoid two tasks colliding on activation-ledger-reader.ts in this shared worktree, which is still a real hazard. If you split, sequence them rather than running them in parallel.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
DEFECT 1 — NARROW THE READER'S INPUT, DO NOT WEAKEN THE GUARD. The guard at activation-ledger-reader.ts:61 means "exactly one ACTIVATION record per aggregate", but `answerReplayed` hands it EVERY event on the aggregate regardless of type, so any foreign event on that aggregate reads as ambiguity. The fix is to select the activation events before the exactly-one check — the reader already knows the discriminator, `ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVENT_TYPE`, and uses it one line later at :65. Filtering by it preserves the invariant's MEANING (two activation events still refuse) while tolerating a Foundation tail of other types. DoD 2 names exactly this shape: the fix "narrows the reader's input rather than weakening the guard".
Rejected: relaxing `events.length > 1` to "take the first". That silently accepts a genuinely ambiguous aggregate and destroys the guarantee the ledger exists to provide.
Rejected: swapping in `readFoundationActivationHistory` (:161) wholesale. The description floats it, and it is history-aware, but the replay path needs ONE record with exactly-one semantics, not a history. Borrow its filtering discipline, not its return shape.

DEFECT 2 — THE PAGE CAP IS NOT A SAFETY DEVICE, and that is the decisive finding. The obvious worry about deleting `MAX_SCAN_PAGES` is an unbounded loop, but the loop ALREADY has a termination guarantee that does not depend on it: at :258-259 the cursor must strictly advance or the scan returns SCAN_INCOMPLETE (`if (next === null || next <= cursor)`), and at :242 an empty page with `hasMore` also returns SCAN_INCOMPLETE. A non-advancing or lying store therefore terminates the loop on its own. `MAX_SCAN_PAGES = 64` adds NO safety a malicious or broken store could otherwise exploit — it only imposes an arbitrary 6,400-event ceiling on a correct store. So the minimal correct fix is to stop bounding the scan by page count and let the existing cursor-advance guard own termination.

THE DESIGN QUESTION, raised rather than assumed (task rail 4). Even fixed, `scanForEffect` is O(total project events) PER LOOKUP: it reads the GLOBAL stream from cursor 0n and cannot exit early because it must prove uniqueness. Removing the cap makes it CORRECT but not FAST, and on a large project every effect-binding lookup walks the whole store. The right long-term answer is probably a per-effect index or a per-aggregate query. That is a design decision this task must NOT land unannounced — the plan requires the worker to write it down and file it as a follow-up, so correctness lands now and the performance question is owned rather than forgotten.

DEFECT 1 IS LATENT, NOT LIVE — the author's own correction (comment-76869409) says so, having re-measured after two skeptics disagreed: `createFoundationLauncherAuthority` has no caller outside its module, its only composition point `createFoundationClaudeLauncher` (foundation-launch-authority.ts:290) has ZERO callers anywhere including tests, and it is not exported from the daemon root. That changes REPRODUCTION, not priority: the test must construct the aggregate tail directly rather than expecting a live path to produce it.

DEFECT 1, apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-commit.ts:133-157 `answerReplayed`:
    events = store.readEvents(aggregateId);        // :140, EVERY event on the aggregate
    const durable = readActivationLedgerRecord(aggregateId, events);   // :144
and the reader's guard at activation-ledger-reader.ts:60-61:
    if (events.length === 0) return activationLedgerUnknown("ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVIDENCE_ABSENT");
    if (events.length > 1) return activationLedgerUnknown("ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS");
The reader checks the type discriminator at :65 (`event.eventType !== ACTIVATION_LEDGER_EVENT_TYPE`) — AFTER the count guard. So the discriminator needed to filter is already in the module; it is simply applied one step too late for this caller.
On success `answerReplayed` re-seals via `encodeActivationLedgerRecord` and compares digests, refusing ACTIVATION_LEDGER_REPLAY_DIVERGED (:150) — that cross-check is correct and must survive the fix.

DEFECT 2, activation-ledger-reader.ts:
- :107 `const MAX_SCAN_PAGES = 64, SCAN_PAGE_SIZE = 100, MAX_QUERY_CHARS = 400;` -> a 6,400-event ceiling.
- :232-262 `scanForEffect`. Loop `for (let page = 0; page < MAX_SCAN_PAGES; page += 1)` (:237). Reads the GLOBAL stream: `store.readEventsAfter(cursor, SCAN_PAGE_SIZE)` from `cursor = 0n` (:235).
- THE ONLY SUCCESS EXIT is `if (!read.hasMore) return { aggregateId: found, refusal: null };` (:255) — it cannot return early on a hit because it must prove the match UNIQUE (:250-253 refuse FOUNDATION_BINDING_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS on a second distinct aggregateId).
- Fallthrough past the loop: `return no("FOUNDATION_BINDING_SCAN_INCOMPLETE")` (:261).
So past 6,400 global events, `read.hasMore` is still true when the 64 iterations finish and EVERY lookup returns SCAN_INCOMPLETE, permanently, for every effect.

THE TERMINATION GUARANTEE THAT MAKES THE FIX SAFE, and it is independent of the page cap:
- :242 `if (read.hasMore && read.items.length === 0) return no("FOUNDATION_BINDING_SCAN_INCOMPLETE");`
- :258-259 `const next = read.nextCursor; if (next === null || next <= cursor) return no("FOUNDATION_BINDING_SCAN_INCOMPLETE");`
A store that stalls, lies, or fails to advance its cursor terminates the loop through these guards, not through MAX_SCAN_PAGES. The page cap is therefore a false ceiling, not a safety net.

THREE READERS in this file (328 lines total, ALREADY over the 250 target and under the 400 split point — pre-existing, and this task must not push it toward 400): `readActivationLedgerRecord` (:56), `readFoundationActivationHistory` (:161), `readCurrentEffectSessionBinding` (:273).

Test surface already present: activation-ledger-commit.test.ts, activation-ledger-reader.test.ts, activation-ledger-fixtures.ts (test-only, no `.js` bridge — the four production modules each have one).
planningNotes.risks:
THE 6,400-EVENT TEST IS THE EXPENSIVE PART AND THE EASIEST TO FAKE. DoD 3 requires a real file-backed SqliteEventStore driven PAST the boundary, with the count pinned as a LITERAL so a later reduction in page size or page count breaks the test rather than silently shrinking the proof. Two ways it goes wrong: (a) the test uses an in-memory or mocked store and proves nothing about the real pager; (b) the count is derived from `MAX_SCAN_PAGES * SCAN_PAGE_SIZE`, which makes it move with the constant it is supposed to pin — an equivalent-mutant trap. Write the number.

SQLITE HANDLES KILL THE VITEST WORKER. Open the store inside the test and close it in a `finally`; a handle held into teardown takes the worker process down and reads as unrelated infrastructure failure. Insert the 6,400+ events in ONE transaction — 6,400 individual commits will be slow enough to look like a hang, and a drill that hangs reads as a passing guard.

DO NOT BUY SCALE BY DROPPING THE UNIQUENESS PROOF (task rail 1). The scan cannot exit early on a hit; it must keep walking to detect a second distinct aggregate. Any fix that returns on first match trades a correct refusal for a wrong answer, and DoD 4 exists to catch it — a second matching activation PAST the old 6,400 bound must still refuse FOUNDATION_BINDING_EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS.

DO NOT WEAKEN THE EXACTLY-ONE GUARD (defect 1). Relaxing `events.length > 1` to "take the first" makes the replay test pass and destroys the ledger's core guarantee. DoD 2 requires a test proving a genuinely ambiguous aggregate — two ACTIVATION events — still refuses with its exact code and layer.

DEFECT 1 IS LATENT, so the test must CONSTRUCT the multi-event aggregate directly. Do not wait for a live Foundation path to produce the tail: `createFoundationClaudeLauncher` has zero callers, so a test that depends on that path executing will never exercise the defect and will pass vacuously.

THE FILE IS ALREADY AT 328 LINES, over the 250 target and under the 400 split point. That is pre-existing and not this task's to fix, but do not push it toward 400 — if the fix needs meaningful new code, extract a helper module rather than growing this one.

THE PERFORMANCE QUESTION MUST BE RAISED, NOT SOLVED HERE (task rail 4). Removing the cap makes the scan correct and leaves it O(total events) per lookup. File the index/per-aggregate-query decision as a follow-up task and record its id; landing an index unannounced is explicitly forbidden.

DoD 6 requires every EXISTING activation-ledger test to stay green and UNMODIFIED. If one reddens, the fix changed behaviour it should not have.
